first_impression.reaction: My daughter sent me this, so I read it properly. The opening is plain and sensible, no silly slang, and I understood straight away what a 4pm day looks like. It's really written for her, not me, but I kept going because I wanted to see where Nana fits into all of this.

journey.quote: The one time that fixes everything else is sunset at your venue on your date, so look that up first and build the photos, the lighting and the reception entrance around it.
journey.reaction: Good, a practical starting point. I like being told the one thing to do first.

journey.section: The 4pm wedding timeline at a glance
journey.quote: Every clock time on this page is a planning example to adapt, not a rule.
journey.reaction: Honest. Nobody is pretending this is set in stone, which I appreciate.

journey.section: A 4pm wedding timeline with a first look
journey.quote: 3.15pm. Any family photos you are happy to take before the ceremony.
journey.reaction: The lists are easy to read on the iPad. I'd want to know how long my mother would be standing about for the family photos, but at least they're kept short.

journey.section: How sunset shapes a 4pm wedding day
journey.quote: By the end of evening civil twilight, when the centre of the sun is 6 degrees below the horizon, large objects can be seen but no detail can be made out without artificial light.
journey.reaction: This bit lost me a little. Degrees below the horizon is more than I need. The point underneath it is a good one though: put the lights on before it gets dark.

journey.quote: If guests walk between the ceremony and reception spaces outdoors, along garden paths, terraces or a coastal road, move them before then or light the route.
journey.reaction: Yes. This is exactly what worries me. My mother uses a walking frame and a dark garden path is the last thing she needs. I wish it said a word about steps and uneven ground too, not only light.

journey.section: Where the buffer belongs in a 4pm day
journey.quote: Make sure food arrives with the first drink, there is shade or warmth depending on the season, and there is somewhere to sit.
journey.reaction: Somewhere to sit. Thank you. That's the first time older guests are considered, even if not by name.

journey.section: Wedding day timeline for a 2pm ceremony
journey.quote: In warm months, heat is the issue: water at the guests' seats, a covered aisle or a short service.
journey.reaction: Sensible, but this paragraph is long and dense to read. And it's the older guests who suffer most in the heat, which isn't said.

journey.section: Planning a 4pm ceremony at a destination wedding
journey.quote: Is there a quiet fallback if a flight lands late?
journey.reaction: Good practical questions to put to the venue. But there's nothing in the list about access for older or less mobile guests, which is the thing I'd be asking first.

journey.section: Planning a 4pm ceremony at a destination wedding
journey.quote: A Wedded Advisor plans venue, travel, vendors and payments anywhere in the world, works in your time zone, and is your single point of contact from start to finish.
journey.reaction: Single point of contact and working in our time zone is reassuring. 'Payments' makes me want to know more: how are deposits handled, and is the money protected?

journey.section: Plan the day around your light
journey.quote: If you would like to work it through with someone, a Wedded Advisor agrees the fee in writing before any work begins, confirms inclusions in writing before you commit, and quotes in AUD for Australian couples.
journey.reaction: This is the sentence I'd read out to my husband. Fees in writing, AUD quotes. That's what I want to see. I only wish it came with a name and a way to speak to someone.

unanswered_questions: Is the deposit protected, and who holds it when we pay an overseas venue?
Are contracts with overseas venues in English, and are payments made in AUD or the local currency?
Who do I ring if something goes wrong close to the day, given the time difference?
Can I speak to someone on the phone before anything is booked, and who would that person be?
How do venues usually look after older or less mobile guests between the ceremony, drinks and dinner spaces?
Does the Advisor help with travel insurance or with guests who have medical needs abroad?

turn_offs_found.quote: The end of evening nautical twilight, at 12 degrees below the horizon, is dark for normal practical purposes.
turn_offs_found.why: Too technical for me. I don't need the astronomy, just the practical point about lighting and moving guests.

turn_offs_found.quote: The gap before dinner is long, so choose a plan rather than letting it drift: a generous drinks with substantial canapés, an afternoon tea, or a break for guests to return to their rooms before an evening reception. Guests travel in the late morning, so anyone arriving the same day has the least room for a delayed flight or a slow drive.
turn_offs_found.why: Part of a long, packed paragraph. Hard work on an iPad. Not a big problem, but I'd rather it was broken up.

would_share_with: My husband, with the closing paragraph about fees in writing and AUD quotes highlighted
My daughter, to say the lighting and the garden path bit matter for Nana

cta_reaction.quote: If you would like to work it through with someone, a Wedded Advisor agrees the fee in writing before any work begins, confirms inclusions in writing before you commit, and quotes in AUD for Australian couples.
cta_reaction.why: The fee-in-writing promise is what I'm looking for. I'd click to see who these people are, but I wouldn't commit to anything without a phone call, and the page doesn't tell me whether I can ring someone or what happens to deposits.

top_3_changes: Add a destination question about older and less mobile guests (step-free access between spaces, somewhere to sit in shade or warmth during photos). This is the first thing a parent asks.
Mention older guests where heat and dark paths come up, so practical safety reads as considered rather than incidental.
Soften the twilight astronomy: lead with the practical instruction and keep the degrees as a supporting detail, so a non-specialist reader doesn't stall.

suggested_edits.reason: Older and less mobile guests are not mentioned anywhere in the destination questions.
suggested_edits.old: - **The welcome dinner the night before.** How late can it run without taking the edge off the wedding morning? Does it share the venue's curfew?
suggested_edits.new:
- **The welcome dinner the night before.** How late can it run without taking the edge off the wedding morning? Does it share the venue's curfew?
- **Older and less mobile guests.** Is there step-free access between the ceremony, drinks and dinner spaces? Where can they sit in shade or out of the cold while photos are taken?

suggested_edits.reason: Lighting the route is good, but uneven ground and steps matter just as much for a guest with a walking frame.
suggested_edits.old: If guests walk between the ceremony and reception spaces outdoors, along garden paths, terraces or a coastal road, move them before then or light the route.
suggested_edits.new: If guests walk between the ceremony and reception spaces outdoors, along garden paths, terraces or a coastal road, move them before then or light the route, and check it is safe for anyone unsteady on their feet.

suggested_edits.reason: Heat is hardest on older guests; naming them makes the advice feel considered.
suggested_edits.old: In warm months, heat is the issue: water at the guests' seats, a covered aisle or a short service.
suggested_edits.new: In warm months, heat is the issue, especially for older guests: water at the guests' seats, a covered aisle or a short service.

checks.check: Every journey point, turn-off and CTA reaction quotes an exact sentence from the draft
Stayed in character as Margaret, funding mother of the bride reading on an iPad
No invented brand facts; deposit, contract, phone and insurance gaps listed as unanswered questions

Suggested edits are exact old/new strings and add no prices, statistics, 'free', 'last dance', vendor names, fees, on-the-ground staff, transfers, room blocks, availability or implication that the Advisor runs the day
HTML comments and image slots treated as invisible
Payload matches 07-icp schema (top_3_changes max 3, scores 1 to 5)

open_questions.question: Deposit protection, contract language/currency and whether a phone call is offered before booking are unanswered for this persona. Is there an approved, sourced line Wedded Wonderland can use, or should these stay off this timeline post?
